items.title: One field with all endpoint estimates
items.note: planar_field states the lemma with its hypotheses written out (module docstring): F convex (hF); F_* the minimum (IsLeast (range F) Fstar); C nonempty, compact, C ⊆ {F = ℓ}, ℓ > F_*; no nontrivial segment in frontier {F ≤ ℓ} (hstrict); no affine-critical point in C (IsAffineCritical F p is 0 ∈ aff ∂F(p), see isAffineCritical_iff); and hregular, the smooth or regular convex two-branch structure of hypothesis 2 of Theorem art:planar-cluster written as in the TeX and in the coverage of local.tex (F C² on an open V ∋ p, or F = max{f₁, f₂} on an open V ∋ p with f₁, f₂ convex and C² on V, both active at p, ∇f₁(p), ∇f₂(p) linearly independent); regularity_of_literal and literal_of_regularity show it is equivalent to the library's ContDiffAt ℝ 2 F p ∨ ConvexTwoBranchRegularAt F p; 0 < c₁ < c₂ < 1. Conclusion: ∃ U Q w η κ δ C₀ C₁ L, all before the pair (the quantifier order of the last sentence), with U open ⊇ C, Q compact ⊇ closure U, η, κ, δ > 0, C₀, C₁, L ≥ 0. Item 1: 'w defined on a neighborhood of Q and locally Lipschitz' is: w is locally Lipschitz at every point of an open N ⊇ Q (w is a total function); ‖w‖ ≤ B on Q (Euclidean); η ≤ gᵀw(p) and equal pairings for all g ∈ ∂F(p), p ∈ Q. Items 2 and 3 for every eligible pair x, z ∈ U (EligiblePair F c₁ c₂ x z g h: g, h the gradients at x, z, d > 0, c₁d ≤ Δ ≤ d, t ≥ (1-c₂)d, as at energy.tex:234-239) with ‖s‖ < δ, where s = z - x, y = h - g, d = -gᵀs = -dot g (z - x), t = yᵀs = dot (h - g) (z - x) are written out and det(s,·) is pairDet s ·. Proof: the library's PlanarAllPairs.source_all_endpoint_estimates (same construction as the TeX proof; its field is PlanarObjectiveField.field hF χ v), with N from PlanarObjectiveField.exists_open_local_lipschitz_extension and the bound on Q from continuity on the compact Q. The hypotheses that F attains F_*, C ≠ ∅, ℓ > F_* and c₁ < c₂ are not needed by the proof (prefixed _); they are kept because the lemma states them.

Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M38, M39, M40, M41): θ is flagged as a segment parameter (not a normal angle); the numerator of D′/D is identified through D′(θ) = det(s, Dw s); exp(4Ad) for e^{4Ad} (e is also an entry of Dw); the citation of [Bog22] no longer repeats the author; φ′(0) = −d kept on one line; end-of-proof mark. planar_field is proved from the library theorem PlanarAllPairs.source_all_endpoint_estimates, which follows the TeX construction (inverse-function corner charts, finitely many level-ℓ corners, disjoint normal arcs, smooth cutoffs, the joined field, uniform visibility, transversality by compactness, transport by right derivatives, local secant bounds, finite cover); it is not assembled from the display theorems of this module, which state each display under the assumptions of its place in the proof. Undisplayed steps stated in this module: corner_curve (lines 41-44), exists_angle and fieldFormula_periodic (84, 89), transversality_contradiction (140-141), one_sided_comparison (168-173), transport_constants (184-189), same_branch_secant (206-208), crossing_tie_point (210-212), crossing_secant (228-230). Library theorems for other undisplayed steps: nonsmooth_level_isolated (line 50), finite_nonsmooth_on_compact_level (51-56), normalSector_pairing_pos and normalSectors_disjoint (59-65), exists_moving_normalSector_cutoffs (67-70), field_from_actual_cornerCharts and exists_uniform_supports_visibility (96-109), compact_pair_transversality_length (126-141), structured_field_segment_transport and planar_transport_from_right_derivative_budget (143-189), square_bound_of_log_bound (188), compact_uniform_secant (231-233). The literature remarks at lines 120-123 (the formula hn + h_θT is classical; Bogosel) and 204-205 (the estimate underlying cocoercivity; WW) are attributions; the facts used are proved here (tangent_cancellation, branch_cocoercivity). The Lean visibility proof gets the uniform lower bound from compactness of the subdifferential graph rather than the supporting inequality suggested at lines 105-108 (both work). Every step checked holds as written; no discrepancy. Non-vacuity: the examples at the end of the module show that the hypotheses of every display and step theorem hold together for the objective of Theorem art:nonradial-example with C = {p₀}, p₀ = (40/721, 39/721), a tie of two branches (corner data with the curve and field of the proof; a smooth point and eligible pairs; the library construction for disp/012; an eligible pair crossing the switching curve for disp/016-018), except transversality_contradiction, whose assumptions are contradictory by design.

Stated at a nonsmooth point c ∈ C with the two-branch data of hregular at c as variables (open V ∋ c, branches f₁, f₂ convex and C² on V, F = max{f₁, f₂} on V, both active at c, independent gradients), the curve p_j as a variable p with its characterization (p ℓ = c, C² at ℓ, f₁(p(t)) = f₂(p(t)) = t for t near ℓ) and v = deriv p. Conclusion: v is C¹ at ℓ (the 'C¹ velocity') and both pairings equal 1 for t near ℓ. corner_curve proves the preceding claims (the branch-value map x ↦ (f₁(x), f₂(x)) has an invertible derivative at c; the inverse function theorem gives such a C² curve, which near c is the only point where f₁ = f₂), so the assumptions on p can be met.

height χ v t θ is literally the display, for angular cutoffs χ : Fin m → ℝ → ℝ and velocities v : Fin m → ℝ → Vec 2, with n(θ) = normal θ = (cos θ, sin θ). In the Lean construction the angular cutoffs are θ ↦ χ_j(n(θ)) for smooth ambient cutoffs χ_j : ℝ² → ℝ (so they are smooth and 2π-periodic); height_eq_library identifies height with the library's PlanarJoinedFrame.height and PlanarAmbientFrame.height for them.

fieldFormula χ v t θ = h(t,θ)n(θ) + h_θ(t,θ)T(θ) with h_θ = deriv (height χ v t), so the display is w(x) = fieldFormula χ v (F x) θ(x), where θ(x) is any angle with n(θ(x)) = ∇F(x)/‖∇F(x)‖ (exists_angle: such an angle exists when ∇F(x) ≠ 0; fieldFormula_periodic: the formula is 2π-periodic, line 89). field_eq_fieldFormula is the unfolding theorem for the field of the Lean proof, PlanarObjectiveField.field hF χ v (ambient form of the formula at a selected subgradient's unit normal): at every point where F has gradient g, and every θ with n(θ) = g/‖g‖, it equals the displayed formula with the angular cutoffs θ ↦ χ_j(n(θ)).

corner_field_formula is the calculation 'h = nᵀv_j, h_θ = Tᵀv_j, w(x) = v_j(F(x))' at a smooth point whose normal angle has a neighborhood on which χ_j = 1 (the other cutoffs then vanish there, by disjoint supports). corner_field is the neighborhood statement for the field of the proof, at a corner c with its two-branch data and curve as in disp/003: if the ambient cutoff χ_j equals 1 on a neighborhood of the normal arc at c (normalSector of ∇f₁(c), ∇f₂(c), the unit directions of their cone), then near c every subgradient is nonzero with unit normal in the plateau, and w(z) = v_j(F(z)) for all z near c, on both smooth sides and on the switching curve ('Use the same formula on the curve itself', line 96).

At a point x with gradient g ≠ 0, normal angle θ (n(θ) = g/‖g‖) and w(x) = fieldFormula χ v (F x) θ (the definition), with angular cutoffs 0 ≤ χ_j ≤ 1 with disjoint supports and n(θ)ᵀv_j(F(x)) > 0 wherever χ_j(θ) ≠ 0 (the support condition of lines 68-70 at the level F(x)): gᵀw(x) = ‖g‖h(F(x),θ) and ‖g‖h(F(x),θ) > 0.

For C² angular cutoffs, any velocities and any level t, with h = height χ v t (a variable with its definition): the derivative of θ ↦ h(θ)n(θ) + h'(θ)T(θ) at θ is (h(θ) + h''(θ))T(θ). No sign or convexity condition on h.

derivative_triangular: at a point x where F is C² with ∇F(x) ≠ 0, the velocities are C¹ at F(x), and w is given by (art:planar-field-formula) near x (for every angle of the normal), w is differentiable at x, Dw = fderiv ℝ w x maps the tangent line {u : nᵀu = 0} into itself, and with n = ∇F(x)/‖∇F(x)‖, T = rotate n (= T(θ(x))), a = TᵀDwT, b = TᵀDw n, e = nᵀDw n: Dw T = aT and Dw n = bT + en, i.e. the matrix of Dw in the basis (T,n) is [[a,b],[0,e]]. derivative_coefficients_bounded is 'with bounded coefficients': if w is locally Lipschitz on an open N containing the compact buffer Q, one B bounds |a|, |b|, |e| at every point of Q for every unit normal n.

The display is inside a proof by contradiction. transversality_limits states it for sequences x_k, z_k, g_k, h_k with s_k = z_k - x_k → 0, x_k → p ∈ Q, s_k/‖s_k‖ → ŝ, g_k → ḡ, h_k → h̄, ḡ, h̄ ∈ ∂F(p) and ŝ = -w(p)/‖w(p)‖ (the facts derived before the display), d_k = -g_kᵀs_k, t_k = (h_k - g_k)ᵀs_k, with visibility η > 0 and common pairing of w on Q. It does not assume that the pairs are eligible: with eligibility these assumptions are contradictory, which is what the next sentence uses (transversality_contradiction derives False from them). Lean names gbar, hbar, shat. Without eligibility the assumptions are satisfiable: an example at the end of the module gives constant sequences at the smooth point (1/20, 0) of the objective of Theorem art:nonradial-example.

At a segment point q = x + θs of an eligible pair where F is C² with ∇F(q) ≠ 0 and w is given by the formula near q, with n, T, a, b, e as in disp/009 at q and s_T = Tᵀs, s_n = nᵀs: det(T,n) = -1, s = s_T T + s_n n, and det(s, Dw s) = s_n((a - e)s_T + b s_n). det(u,v) is pairDet u v = u₀v₁ - u₁v₀ (columns u, v); the sign is the TeX's.

Under the facts established before the display, for the field of the proof w = PlanarObjectiveField.field hF χ v: w locally Lipschitz on an open N ⊇ Q, Q compact; velocities C¹ at F(p) and the smooth/corner structure (F C² at p, or w = v_j∘F near p) for every p ∈ Q; visibility η on Q; transversality κ on the segments of eligible pairs in U with ‖s‖ < δ. Conclusion: one A ≥ 0, chosen before the pair, such that for every such pair, with q(θ) = x + θs, φ(θ) = F(q(θ)), D(θ) = det(s, w(q(θ))), H(θ) = log|D(θ)| and d = -gᵀs (variables with their definitions) and 0 ≤ θ < 1: H has the right derivative H'_+(θ) = derivWithin H (Ioi θ) θ (HasDerivWithinAt on Ici θ), |H'_+(θ)| ≤ A|φ'_+(θ)| and A|φ'_+(θ)| ≤ A(φ'_+(θ) + 2d), with φ'_+(θ) = derivWithin φ (Ioi θ) θ.

The display defines the two comparison functions u = σ(H(θ) - H(0)) - A(φ(θ) - φ(0) + 2dθ), σ = ±1. The claim made about them ('Both start at zero and have nonpositive right derivative', and the one-sided comparison then gives u(1) ≤ 0) is comparison_functions, for each sign, assuming D continuous and nonzero on [0,1] (transversality) and the bound of disp/012 for this pair with the constant A. one_sided_comparison states the comparison fact of lines 170-175 (continuous u on [0,1] with u'_+ ≤ 0 on [0,1) has u(1) ≤ u(0)).

Under the assumptions of disp/013 (without the sign); φ(1) ≤ φ(0) is derived from Armijo and c₁ > 0. transport_constants proves the following undisplayed claims (lines 186-191): λ = D(1)/D(0) > 0, w(z) = λw(x) + βs, |log λ| ≤ 2Ad and, for d ≤ 1, λ² ≤ e^{4Ad} ≤ 1 + (e^{4A} - 1)d.

The larger convex chart is an open convex V on which f is convex and C², with ∇f M-Lipschitz in the Euclidean norm (M > 0); 'sufficiently close buffered endpoints' are x, z in a set B whose Euclidean ρ-balls lie in V, with ‖z - x‖ < ρ. The eligible pair and the same-branch conditions f(x) = F(x), f(z) = F(z) are hypotheses (not needed: the inequality holds for all such x, z). Proof as in the TeX (tangent plane at x, Euclidean descent estimate at z for the step -(∇f(z) - ∇f(x))/M, which stays in V since its length is at most ‖z - x‖). same_branch_secant proves the next sentences (lines 208-210): when also ∇f(x) = g and ∇f(z) = h, the bracket is at most t, and (yᵀw(z))²/t ≤ 2MG² if ‖w(z)‖ ≤ G.

Two-branch chart: open convex V with F = max{f₀, f₁} on V (Lean f : Fin 2 → Vec 2 → ℝ, so the TeX's branches i, j are indices of Fin 2), f_i convex and C² on V, ∇f_i M-Lipschitz and bounded by H_b on V; w B_w-Lipschitz and bounded by G on V, with equal pairing with all subgradients on V (facts established before; Euclidean norms). Conclusion: one A₁ ≥ 0 such that every eligible pair x, z ∈ V with branch i active at x and a different branch j active at z has |yᵀw(z)| ≤ A₁‖s‖ (the proof gives A₁ = 2MG + 2H_bB_w). crossing_tie_point proves the preceding claims (lines 212-214): a tie point p on the segment with (∇f_j(p) - ∇f_i(p))ᵀw(p) = 0.
In the setting of disp/016, with r = ∇f_j(z) - ∇f_j(x), s, y, d, t as variables with their definitions: ‖r‖ ≤ M‖s‖ (the claim before the display) and the two displayed identities.

'Their inverse bound' is A₂ ≥ 0 with ‖u‖ ≤ A₂(|∇f₀(x')ᵀu| + |∇f₁(x')ᵀu|) for all u and all x' in the chart (Euclidean ‖u‖); its existence near a corner is the library's eventually_actual_pair_control (sup norm, which differs from the Euclidean norm by at most a factor 2). Both displayed inequalities are proved. crossing_secant proves the next sentences (lines 230-232): if A₂ > 0 and A₂M‖s‖ ≤ 1/2, then t ≥ a₀‖s‖ with a₀ = 1/(2A₂(1 + 2/(1 - c₂))) > 0 and (yᵀw(z))²/t ≤ A₁²‖s‖/a₀.

items.anchor: This appendix supplies the geometric ingredient used in Theorem~\ref{art:planar-cluster}.
items.note: The geometric ingredient is Lemma art:planar-field (planar_field); the proof of Theorem art:planar-cluster (A/local/proof/005) uses it at local.tex:247-256. Corrected on 15 October 2026 (M34): the sentence before that display (local.tex:249) now takes the pairs with d ≤ 1, the lemma's restriction; before, the display (local.tex:254) stated λ² ≤ 1 + Ld without it (the restriction holds anyway for the sufficiently close pairs of that proof, since d = -gᵀs ≤ ‖g‖‖s‖ with gradients bounded near the cluster set; the coverage of local.tex takes δ ≤ 1/G).

items.anchor: The construction applies near a compact regular part of one positive level.
items.note: Summarizes the setting of planar_field: C is a nonempty compact subset of the level {F = ℓ} with ℓ > F_*, all of whose points are regular (smooth or regular two-branch) and not affine critical; U, Q and the field are near C.

items.anchor: It does not assume that the BFGS iterates converge to one point of that level.
items.note: planar_field has no BFGS run, iterate or matrix among its hypotheses, and C is an arbitrary nonempty compact subset of the level, not a single limit point.
